title: Leaving out to-infinitives
summary: Опущение инфинитивов с сохранением to (I'd love to, I used to), сохранение be и have (used to be, would love to have), if you want.
ru:
## Что опускаем, а что нет
Если после глагола (или прилагательного), который требует инфинитива с *to*, смысловая часть уже известна, мы опускаем **сам инфинитив**, но **оставляем *to***.
> A: Are you coming to the party? B: I'd love **to**. — С удовольствием (приду).
> He didn't help, although I asked him **to**. — ...хотя я просил.
> You can stay if you want **to**.
> I didn't call her, although I meant **to**.
Это очень частая конструкция. В русском мы просто обрываем фразу («Хотел бы…»). В английском нельзя: ~~I'd love.~~ ~~I don't want.~~ → I'd love **to**. I don't want **to**.

## Где употребляется
**Глаголы:** want, would like / love / hate, hope, try, expect, intend, plan, mean, promise, refuse, agree, decide, choose, forget, **ask / tell / advise / want somebody**.
**Выражения:** be going to, have to, ought to, used to, need to, be able to, be supposed to, be happy / glad / afraid to.
> A: Did you tell him? B: No, I was going **to**, but I forgot.
> I don't smoke now, but I used **to**.
> He didn't clean the kitchen, though he was supposed **to**.
Отрицание тоже сохраняется: *He told me not **to**. · I decided not **to**.*

## Исключения: if you want / like
В придаточном с *if* после **want** и **like** допустимо опустить и *to*: *Stay here if you want.* / *Come along if you like.* С *would like* такого нет: *I'll come if you'd like me to.*

## Оставляем be и have
Если опущенный инфинитив — **to be** (в том числе пассивный), *be* нужно оставить:
> She isn't as confident as she used to **be**. — не как раньше.
> I'm not a manager, but I'd like to **be**.
> He wasn't invited, but he wanted to **be**.
Если опущен **перфектный** инфинитив, *have* тоже остаётся:
> A: Did you see the match? B: No, but I'd love to **have**. — Нет, но с радостью бы посмотрел.
Сравните: *used to* → *I don't smoke now, but I used **to***; *used to be* → *She isn't as shy as she used to **be***.

## Нельзя
- Если инфинитив **не понятен из контекста**, опускать его нельзя.
- После обычных глаголов без *to* (*can, will, should* и т.п.) — это уже ситуация юнита 67: *I can't, but she can.*
- ~~I'd love to go, but I can't to.~~ → I'd love to go, but I **can't**. (после модального *to* не нужен)

## Тонкости стиля
Короткий ответ *I'd love to.* — тёплое согласие. Холодный отказ: *I'd like to, but I can't.* Сравните с твёрдым *I don't want to.* — часто воспринимается резко. Мягче: *I'd rather not.* (без *to*).

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~A: Are you coming? B: I want.~~ → **I want to.**
- ~~She isn't as brave as she used to.~~ → She isn't as brave as she used to **be**.
- ~~I didn't phone, although I was going.~~ → ...although I was going **to**.
- ~~He asked me to stay, but I didn't want~~ → ...I didn't want **to**.
en:
## What we leave out and what we keep
If the meaning is clear, we can omit the infinitive after a verb or adjective that takes *to*, but we **keep *to***.
> A: Are you coming to the party? B: I'd love **to**.
> He didn't help, although I asked him **to**.
> You can stay if you want **to**.
> I didn't call her, although I meant **to**.
In Russian you can simply break off ("Хотел бы…"). In English you cannot: ~~I'd love.~~ ~~I don't want.~~ → I'd love **to**. I don't want **to**.

## Where it is used
**Verbs:** want, would like / love / hate, hope, try, expect, intend, plan, mean, promise, refuse, agree, decide, choose, forget, **ask / tell / advise / want somebody**.
**Expressions:** be going to, have to, ought to, used to, need to, be able to, be supposed to, be happy / glad / afraid to.
> A: Did you tell him? B: No, I was going **to**, but I forgot.
> I don't smoke now, but I used **to**.
> He didn't clean the kitchen, though he was supposed **to**.
The negative stays too: *He told me not **to**. · I decided not **to**.*

## An exception: if you want / like
In an *if*-clause after **want** and **like** we can also drop *to*: *Stay here if you want.* / *Come along if you like.* This is not possible with *would like*: *I'll come if you'd like me to.*

## Keep be and have
When the omitted infinitive is **to be** (including the passive), keep *be*:
> She isn't as confident as she used to **be**.
> I'm not a manager, but I'd like to **be**.
> He wasn't invited, but he wanted to **be**.
When the omitted infinitive is **perfect**, keep *have*:
> A: Did you see the match? B: No, but I'd love to **have**.
Compare: *I don't smoke now, but I used **to*** and *She isn't as shy as she used to **be***.

## Not allowed
- If the infinitive is not clear from the context, do not omit it.
- After modals there is no *to* at all (see unit 67): ~~I'd love to go, but I can't to.~~ → ...but I **can't**.

## Style
*I'd love to.* is a warm acceptance. A polite refusal: *I'd like to, but I can't.* A flat *I don't want to.* can sound rude; softer is *I'd rather not.*

## Common mistakes
- ~~A: Are you coming? B: I want.~~ → **I want to.**
- ~~She isn't as brave as she used to.~~ → She isn't as brave as she used to **be**.
- ~~I didn't phone, although I was going.~~ → ...although I was going **to**.
structure:
## Что остаётся
| Исходная конструкция | Сокращённо | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| want to + V | want to | I didn't go, but I wanted to. |
| would love to + V | would love to | I'd love to. |
| be going to + V | be going to | I was going to. |
| used to + V | used to | I used to. |
| not to + V | not to | I decided not to. |
| to be + ... | to be | She wanted to be. |
| to have + V3 | to have | I'd love to have. |

## Формулы
> **Verb + to** (инфинитив опущен): *I'd love to. · I meant to. · I have to.*
> **if you want / like** (без to): *Stay if you want.*
> **used to be** (be остаётся): *She isn't as shy as she used to be.*

## Нельзя
| Неверно | Верно |
|---|---|
| ~~I'd love.~~ | I'd love to. |
| ~~I used to.~~ (вместо used to be) | I used to be. |
| ~~I can't to.~~ | I can't. |
